extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors and news organizations covering elections and political campaigns
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for reporting on elections — what to cover, how to categorize coverage, editorial independence and truthfulness standards, and reforms to improve public-interest journalism during campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voters' right to be informed
rubrics_metrics.description: Voters' right to be informed about candidates and platforms
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage should ensure voters receive clear, accessible information about who the candidates are, their platforms and what those policies mean in practice. Prioritize material that helps voters make informed decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contestants' right to communicate
rubrics_metrics.description: Contestants' right to communicate platforms with non-discriminatory media access
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media should provide fair opportunities for candidates/parties to present their messages without unlawful or arbitrary discrimination; apply consistent access rules and disclose any deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media's right to inform and express opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Media's right to inform and express opinion on public-interest issues
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists and outlets retain the right to investigate, report and editorialize on matters of public interest while maintaining transparency about opinion versus news content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality vs. Equity Frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: Equality: each party/candidate receives same time/space; Equity: proportional access based on uniform criteria (parliamentary seats, candidate count)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide newsroom allocation approach explicitly: equality (equal time/space) or equity (proportional access using objective measures). Document and justify the chosen approach to avoid perceptions of bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voter relevance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize stories and angles that materially affect how voters decide (policy impacts, candidate positions, practical effects). De-emphasize items unlikely to influence electoral choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate viability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage may give more attention to candidates with demonstrated viability (polling, party support, funding), but remain transparent about criteria used and avoid creating momentum artificially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue salience
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus reporting on issues that matter to voters (economy, healthcare, security) rather than trivial or purely sensational items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthy event
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsworthy event — debate, scandal, gaffe, endorsement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report on verifiable events with clear public-interest relevance. Avoid elevating unverified or manufactured incidents; explain context and significance rather than amplifying drama.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Platform clarity — explaining what candidates promise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain policy proposals clearly and concretely, including implications, feasibility and trade-offs. Use fact-checking and expert commentary to assess claims and promises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting logistics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide practical information voters need to participate (registration deadlines, polling locations, voting methods, ID requirements). Make this information accessible and repeated as election day approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voter suppression / fraud allegations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate and report allegations of suppression or fraud with care: verify claims, explain evidence, avoid uncritical repetition of false or misleading accusations, and detail remedies or official responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polling significance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report poll results with methodological context (sample size, margin of error, methodology, sponsor) and avoid overinterpreting small or non-representative polls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Money in politics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow and explain campaign finance flows, donors, and spending patterns. Clarify legal frameworks and any impacts on policy or access; disclose limitations of available data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Down-ballot impact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how top-ticket races and issues affect lower-level contests and governance outcomes; give attention to local races with tangible effects on voters' lives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct categorization of content
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinct Categorization — News stories; Analyses; Opinions / editorials; Paid political advertisements (clearly labeled)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label content clearly so audiences distinguish factual reporting, analysis, opinion and paid political ads. Paid political advertisements must be clearly identified and separated from editorial content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence standards for journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Independence Standards — Journalists avoid personal political activity; Disclose any past political work; Editorial firewall from owner's preferences
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should refrain from overt political activities (donations, petitions, campaigning) that compromise objectivity. Disclose relevant past political engagements. Newsrooms must maintain editorial independence from owners and advertisers, documenting policies and firewalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth-and-fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Truth-and-Fairness — Fact-check claims (especially candidate statements); Don't amplify lies as both-sides; Provide context for claims; Update when facts emerge
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify candidate statements and assertions before publication; contextualize disputed claims rather than presenting 'he said/she said' false equivalence. Issue corrections and updates promptly as new facts are confirmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit political newsworthiness signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit Newsworthiness Criteria for Politics — Power transitions; Conflict / horse race; Personality drama; Policy substance; Process integrity; Suppression and access; Money flows; Polling shifts; Endorsements; Scandal / opposition research; Voter sentiment; Local race significance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware these implicit signals often drive editorial choices. Recognize tendency to over-cover horse-race and personality drama and under-cover policy substance and governance implications. Use this list to audit and balance coverage priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reform recommendations for election coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique — Election coverage often privileges horse-race and gaffes over substantive policy. Reform calls for issue-driven coverage; Voter-needs-first framing; Avoid amplifying disinformation; Focus on what matters for governance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt newsroom practices to shift emphasis: commission issue-focused reporting, center stories on voter needs and governance impacts, implement stronger fact-checking against disinformation, and set editorial metrics that reward policy depth over sensationalism.
